_doc: Review policy read by review_gate.py. CI reads this file from the PR's base ref as merged there (git show origin/<base>:...), never from the PR head, so a PR cannot remove itself from the list; if the base ref has no copy it uses the trusted default-branch checkout. second_family_paths: fnmatch globs ("*" also matches "/"); a diff touching any of them needs a passing review (CLEAN, or FINDINGS disposed) from TWO different model families before the review check goes green. See docs/operations/github-workflow-conventions.md#second-family-review.
_boundary: Listed: files whose main job is an authentication or authorisation decision, or the wiring that configures or mounts one (mcp_server.py, mcp_listen_config.py, the middleware step list, the BEAM routers that mount the auth plugs), and the shared classifiers every gate consults (decorators.py: which calls need identity; stakes_table.py: which need a governance verdict), plus the review gate itself. updates/phases.py is listed despite its size because it holds the main strict-identity write gate (the caller-proven check for sync_state and the no-implicit-identity refusal); Cost, measured 2026-09-27 over the previous 60 days: the whole list matches 170 of 622 commits that touch src/, elixir/ or scripts/dev/ (27%), 12% of all commits. Deliberately NOT listed: large multi-purpose files that contain a single check (http_routes/sentinel.py, mcp_server_std.py, dialectic_protocol.py, mcp_handlers/wave3a_probe.py, mcp_handlers/consolidated.py); listing them would put most of the codebase under the rule. Also NOT listed: modules that sign records for integrity rather than gate access (dialectic_receipt.py, skill_attestations.py). Audited 2026-09-27 across src/ and elixir/ (the BEAM services' bearer plugs and the lease plane's identity-binding gate are listed; their clients, which only present a token, are not) by grepping for strict-identity refusals, compare_digest, CSRF, WebAuthn and trusted-network checks, then for signing, attestation, credential minting and verification, and reading each candidate's module docstring. A dispose --emit or hand-rendered record from a TRUSTED author is not verified beyond its shape; the rule guards against honest single-family review, not against a maintainer who could equally post a false CLEAN.
